author: Claude (autonomous PI, second host)
stage: LUCID vs fixed DR vs no DR, from scratch, single motion

budget_decision.evidence: The no-DR baseline ran 13,245 iterations. Capability metrics plateau early: episode length 183.2 at window 4001-4500 vs 187.4 at 12501-13000 (+2.3% over 9,000 further iterations), and time_out 0.9703 -> 0.9921 (+2.2 pts). Reward keeps creeping (15.08 -> 18.30, +21%) at 0.3-1.3%/500it, which is tracking PRECISION improving, not capability. Plateau reward sd over the last 1,000 iterations is 0.359 on a mean of 18.279 (cv 2.0%), so a 500-window mean has se ~0.09% of the mean and a 0.5%/window criterion sits well above noise.
budget_decision.why_not_20000: 20,000 was the baseline's configured horizon, not a measured requirement. At B=8000 every capability metric is within ~1% of its 13,000-iteration value, and the campaign costs 66 GPU-hours instead of 165.
budget_decision.why_not_4000: DR arms train on a harder distribution and should converge later than the no-DR control. B=8000 is double the iteration at which the control's capability metrics plateaued, so a DR arm gets slack the control did not need.
budget_decision.equal_budget: Every arm and every seed gets exactly B=8000 -- equal iterations, equal environment interactions (8000 x 1024 x 24 = 1.97e8 transitions per cell), equal wall-clock. The user's directive was 'converged AND at least the same training time as the baseline'; equal-B satisfies both without handing a slower arm more compute.

convergence_rule.computable_from: the training log alone, via RL.parse_run_log
convergence_rule.rule: With W=500 non-overlapping windows from iteration 1, let M_k be the window mean of 'Mean rewards' and d_k = (M_k - M_{k-1})/|M_{k-1}|. An (arm, seed) is CONVERGED at B iff there exists k with 500k <= B such that d_k, d_{k-1}, d_{k-2} are all < 0.005, AND that arm's own max window-mean time_out >= 0.5x its own maximum, AND its max window-mean episode length >= 2x its first-window mean.
convergence_rule.liveness_is_arm_relative: An absolute time_out floor would stamp a DR arm FAILED for training on a harder distribution. Both constants (0.5x, 2x) are chosen and declared here.
convergence_rule.if_an_arm_is_not_converged: the headline reads 'at equal budget B=8000', that arm's result is a LOWER bound, and the deficit is reported as a learning-speed finding, not a policy-quality finding.

design.task: walk_hands_on_back_loop_002__A066_M, one 4.03 s clip, adaptation partition, zero dev overlap

arms.off: no event-manager DR. The control. NOT 'no randomization': the motion command term randomizes every reset regardless of lambda.
arms.fixed: full six-channel envelope at lambda=1 from iteration 0
arms.lucid_rg: gap-gated PI controller with the RELATIVE return guard
arms.lucid_s4_rg: the same plus a 4-stratum intensity mixture across environments

design.guard_choice_disclosure: plain `lucid` uses an absolute return floor of 8.0. The no-DR baseline crosses 8.0 at iteration 975, and replaying the controller on the baseline's own traces gives ~499 guard trips with lambda pinned near 0.02. The relative guard was therefore chosen for the LUCID arm AFTER simulating both on baseline traces. That is a forking path and is declared rather than hidden.

hypotheses.H0_instrument: GATE. On the 512-alias replicate panel at num_envs=512, evaluating the baseline checkpoint at phys_000, the receipt must report motion_count=512 and zero censoring. If H0 fails, no arm is evaluated and no endpoint is reported.
hypotheses.H1_lambda: MECHANISM, evaluated before any endpoint. H1a: lucid_rg reaches lambda>=0.95 by iteration 500 and stays, with <=2 guard trips -> any LUCID result is reported as 'a brief ramp then fixed DR', and the gap feedback is credited with the ramp rate only. H1b: final lambda in [0.4,0.9] with >=3 trips -> the controller is genuinely modulating and a result may be attributed to the schedule. Neither (lambda<=0.05 throughout, or >5 trips/1000it sustained) -> both guards are mis-scaled in this regime, and that is the finding.
hypotheses.H2_fixed_learnable: fixed is LIVE at B iff its own max window-mean time_out >= 0.10 and its max window-mean episode length >= 2x its first window. If fixed is not LIVE, 'LUCID beats fixed DR' is a win over an arm that never learned and must be reported that way.
hypotheses.H3_primary: On the physics-only ladder (phys_000/050/100/125/150, latency pinned to 0), trapezoidal AUC of mean per-episode progress, normalised by the lambda span. C1: lucid_rg - off. C2: lucid_rg - fixed. Paired by training seed, Holm-corrected across the two.
hypotheses.H4_latency: SECONDARY. Latency-only ladder AUC over 0/10/20/30/40 ms at nominal physics -- the axis on which the no-DR control has zero training exposure.

statistics.unit_of_analysis: the TRAINING SEED. Per-episode n=512 quantifies episode noise for one trained policy and says nothing about the variability of the training procedure, which is the estimand. Two arms compared at one seed each with n=512 gives a tiny interval entirely confounded with seed -- the most likely way to manufacture a false LUCID win.
statistics.report_both: the within-seed episode CI (precision) and the across-seed CI (the claim). Only the second supports a directional claim.
statistics.no_wilcoxon: at 3 seeds the minimum two-sided p is 0.25; it cannot reach significance and will not be reported as if it could.

if_lucid_loses: Report it as the headline. The programme has already published that the latent gap does not rank DR channels by harm, that an absolute return guard is not scale-portable, and that a population return contaminates a focus-only controller. A fourth negative -- that gap-gated DR scheduling does not beat fixed DR when learning from scratch -- is a result, and the contribution is the diagnosis plus the audit protocol.
